cover.sub: The chipmaker says the leaked data matched records held by a cloud service provider.

slides.title: What TSMC confirmed
slides.body: In a 12 Nov statement filed with the SEC, TSMC said some current and former employees' data was made available on an external website without authorization. It says it has found no evidence its own systems were compromised.

slides.title: Where it came from
slides.body: TSMC verified the data matches data held in a cloud service provider's systems, and says it is unrelated to operations or customer data. The provider isn't named. TSMC is working with it, investigators and an outside security firm.

slides.title: Why it still matters
slides.body: Samples reportedly held names, national ID numbers and bank details (unconfirmed). That's enough for convincing payroll or bank phishing aimed at staff, even with your own network untouched.

items.x_text:
GitHub CI secret stealer: an attacker used 4,837 hijacked accounts to plant it in 1,806+ repos, per Aikido Security. It grabs Actions secrets and tokens, then swaps OIDC tokens for AWS, GCP and Azure sessions. Rotate every secret.

#SupplyChain #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
How one stolen GitHub login becomes keys to your cloud. ☁️

What The Hacker News reported (12 Nov), citing Aikido Security and SafeDep:
→ An attacker used stolen credentials for 4,837 GitHub accounts to plant a CI secret stealer in repos those accounts could write to
→ Aikido says it ran in at least 1,806 repositories; SafeDep counted 8,093 repos receiving malicious commits
→ Red path: hijacked account → commit adds the stealer to a workflow (or an npm postinstall hook) → CI runs it → Actions secrets, GITHUB_TOKEN, cloud and AI keys go out
→ It can swap CI OIDC tokens for AWS, GCP or Azure sessions, then create IAM access keys or rewrite trust policies
→ Aikido: any account that opened a test PR is compromised, even if the stealer never ran

If you were hit: revoke the account's tokens, OAuth grants, SSH keys and sessions, turn on 2FA, rotate every secret the repo can read, and hunt for wfx-* cloud sessions and federated credentials you didn't create.

items.x_text:
Apache HTTP Server CVE-2026-119618: unauthenticated RCE in mod_http2, CVSS 9.8 per Red Hat, affects 2.4.55 to 2.4.70, including servers patched in May. Fix: 2.4.71. No in-the-wild exploitation reported yet.

#Apache #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
Patched Apache's HTTP/2 bug in May? You're still exposed. 🌐

What The Hacker News reported (12 Nov):
→ CVE-2026-119618 is a critical flaw in mod_http2 of Apache HTTP Server: unauthenticated remote code execution on servers with HTTP/2 enabled
→ CVSS 9.8 per Red Hat; affects 2.4.55 through 2.4.70, so servers on 2.4.67 (May's HTTP/2 fix) are still affected
→ Fixed in Apache 2.4.71; standalone mod_h2 has no fixed release
→ Red Hat says public research demonstrated a reliable exploit; Wiz said no in-the-wild exploitation had been reported
→ Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, and by Google Cloud Vulnerability Research

Patch now: upgrade to 2.4.71 or your distro's fixed package. Can't yet? Wiz advises removing h2 and h2c from the Protocols directive (leave 'Protocols http/1.1'), server-wide and in every virtual host.
